scan.name: Sinexis Scan
scan.summary: Outside-in scans for IPs, domains, and mobile builds, with schedules that diff each run and named assets.
scan.metaTitle: Sinexis Scan — exposure scan with scheduled attach
scan.metaDescription: Outside-in scans for IPs, domains, and mobile builds. Schedule each target, diff every run, and keep assets under names your team already uses.
scan.intro: Scan is the exposure surface. You point it at a host, domain, or mobile build you already operate, and it reports what the internet can see. Scheduled attach keeps the result current instead of leaving one forgotten report.
whatItDoes: Scans IPs, domains, and mobile builds from the outside and reports ports, TLS, headers, permissions, and known CVEs.
Schedules a target on an interval and diffs each run against the previous one.
Keeps IPs, domains, and apps in a named asset registry with the plan cap shown.
doesNotDo: Does not log into the host or read files from inside the machine.
Does not test application business logic or booking flows.
Does not offer unlimited assets; each plan has a hard cap.

steps.title: Connect
steps.body: Pick one IP, domain, or mobile build you own and start a run.

steps.title: Attach
steps.body: Set the interval that matches how often the infrastructure changes.

steps.title: Prove
steps.body: Read the diff, then hand the report to a client or an auditor.

requirements: Scan only hosts, domains, and apps you own or are authorized in writing to test.
Asset counts follow the hard cap on the account plan.

guard.name: Sinexis Guard
guard.summary: One wazuh-agent per VM for machine inventory and critical alerts. Not a SIEM console.
guard.metaTitle: Sinexis Guard — inventory and alerts on the box
guard.metaDescription: One wazuh-agent per VM reports inventory and critical alerts. SIEM log search is available by request and never included.
guard.intro: Guard is the thin agent view. One wazuh-agent per VM reports what is installed and running, then raises critical alerts. Log search and cases are a by-request add-on.

capabilityNotes.siem: By request. Log search and cases are enabled per account; never included in the Guard plan.

whatItDoes: Reports installed packages and running services from one wazuh-agent per VM.
Raises critical alerts when the machine reports a change that matters.
Enrolls the host into one organization, with one agent per machine.
doesNotDo: Is not a SIEM console. Log search and cases are by request.
Does not ship a second agent; Host Protect is a helper on the same machine.
Does not provide a staffed incident response team.

steps.title: Enroll
steps.body: Install one wazuh-agent on the VM and enroll it to your organization.

steps.title: Report
steps.body: The agent sends inventory and critical events.

steps.title: Review
steps.body: Read hosts and alerts on the Guard page.

requirements: One wazuh-agent per VM, enrolled to one organization.
SIEM log search and cases are by request; they are never included in Guard.
Host Protect is a separate add-on that requires this agent.

host.name: Sinexis Host Protect
host.summary: An on-box helper for web malware, and a WAF that runs in your own nginx.
host.metaTitle: Sinexis Host Protect + WAF — on-box and in your nginx
host.metaDescription: Host Protect is an add-on that requires a Guard agent and returns empty on a clean disk. Host WAF runs in your nginx on Pro and Multi.
host.intro: Host Protect reads web roots through a helper on the machine that already runs the Guard agent. Host WAF adds detection and protection inside your own nginx. Both are add-ons with plan gates.

capabilityNotes.hostProtect: Host add-on. Requires a Guard agent on the same VM. Returns empty on a clean disk.
capabilityNotes.hostWaf: Pro and Multi. Runs in your nginx, never on the Sinexis edge.

whatItDoes: Reads web directories through a helper and flags files that match malware rules.
Runs WAF detection and protection in the customer's nginx.
Shows an honest empty result when the disk is clean.
doesNotDo: Does not install itself. Host Protect is an add-on and needs a Guard agent on the same VM.
WAF does not run on the Sinexis edge; the snippet goes into your own nginx.
Does not invent malware hits when the disk is clean.

steps.title: Install
steps.body: Make sure the Guard agent is active, then install the Host Protect helper on the same VM.

steps.title: Scan
steps.body: Run the web-directory check and review the result.

steps.title: Protect
steps.body: Enable the WAF rules in your nginx on a supported plan.

requirements: Host add-on. Requires a Guard agent on the same VM. Returns empty on a clean disk.
Pro and Multi. Runs in your nginx, never on the Sinexis edge.

uptime.name: Sinexis Uptime
uptime.summary: HTTP, TCP, DNS, and heartbeat probes, plus a public status page with plan gates.
uptime.metaTitle: Sinexis Uptime — reachability probes and status page
uptime.metaDescription: HTTP, TCP, DNS, and heartbeat probes from outside. Publish a public status page on the plans that support it.
uptime.intro: Uptime hits a URL, TCP port, DNS record, or heartbeat from outside and records when it stops answering. The public status page uses a customer slug, with a clear plan gate.

capabilityNotes.statusPage: Publish on Pro, Multi, and Enterprise. Custom hostname on Multi and Enterprise.

whatItDoes: Monitors HTTP, TCP, DNS, and heartbeat targets from outside.
Records when the target stops answering and keeps the outage history.
Publishes a public status page on a customer slug.
doesNotDo: Does not read CVEs or scan the host.
Does not promise an uptime guarantee.
Does not publish a status page on every plan; publishing is gated by plan.

steps.title: Add
steps.body: Register the URL, TCP port, DNS record, or heartbeat you want to watch.

steps.title: Watch
steps.body: Probes run from outside and record when the service stops answering.

steps.title: Publish
steps.body: Turn on the public status page on a supported plan.

requirements: Publish on Pro, Multi, and Enterprise. Custom hostname on Multi and Enterprise.

ai-gateway.name: Sinexis AI Gateway
ai-gateway.summary: One wallet and API keys per organization for your team's models. Beta, by request.
ai-gateway.metaTitle: Sinexis AI Gateway — wallet and keys per organization
ai-gateway.metaDescription: Beta. One wallet and API keys per organization for your team's models. Access is requested and enabled per account.
ai-gateway.intro: AI Gateway puts one wallet and one set of API keys around the models your team uses. Access is still Beta and requested per account.

capabilityNotes.aiGateway: Beta. Request access; wallet and keys are issued per org.

whatItDoes: Provides one wallet per organization for model usage.
Issues API keys scoped to the organization.
doesNotDo: Is not generally available; access is Beta and requested per account.
Does not bundle credits with an account.
Does not replace your model provider's bill.

steps.title: Request
steps.body: Create an account, then request AI Gateway access.

steps.title: Enable
steps.body: The wallet and keys are issued for your organization.

steps.title: Connect
steps.body: Use those keys from your team's application.

requirements: Beta. Request access; wallet and keys are issued per org.
